predictions.experiment: Accuracy of self-opened plain answers minus cued accuracy on the same problems. This theory predicts about 0. The continuous-entropy / easy-problem-marker rival predicts self-opened answers fall clearly short of cued answers on the same problems, about -0.15.
predictions.recipe: Files: S3 T3.jsonl (s3://pg-lineage-769063704696/results/rlneurons/r4/modal_t3-01/t3/T3.jsonl, plain base, T 1.0) and studies/rlneurons/results/rln4/t1_t2_items-01/per_problem.json. For each T3 row, compute grader v3 with studies/rlneurons/grader/rln4_grader_v3.py from text and gold (rows with cap_hit true keep the score v3 gives; an empty extraction counts 0). Mark a T3 row self-opened if the first 60 characters of its text field contain the substring '\nOkay' (newline immediately followed by 'Okay'). Let S = problem_index values of self-opened T3 rows. A = mean v3 score of T3 rows in S. B = mean of t1_right over the per_problem.json entries whose problem_index is in S. Report D = A - B. Problems missing from either file are dropped from S before both means.
predictions.note: Files: runs/theory-tests/s3/T3.jsonl (fetched from s3://pg-lineage-769063704696/results/rlneurons/r4/modal_t3-01/t3/T3.jsonl, 500 rows, one per problem_index, sample 0) and studies/rlneurons/results/rln4/t1_t2_items-01/per_problem.json (500 entries). The grade is rln4_lib.grade_v3(gold, text)['score_v3'], which is the function rln4_grader_v3.py calls. An extraction of None scores 0, and cap hits keep their score. Main reading: '\nOkay' (a real newline) lies fully inside text[:60]. alt_measured: the regex \n\s*Okay with its match starting before character 60 (it also allows whitespace between the newline and Okay, and an occurrence that runs past character 60). Risks: 21 T3 rows have empty text (n_generated 1). They are never self-opened, so they do not enter S. T3 text holds only the generation (prefix_kind none), so the detector sees no prompt text. B is t1_right as stored, which the inventory says is grader v3. A is regraded from the text, so any grader-version drift would affect A only. S comes from one sample per problem, so A is noisy, and selecting on self-opening can pick easier problems. That selection is part of the design, not a bug. The script prints one diagnostic line (n_S) before the final JSON line.

predictions.experiment: Length of self-opened plain answers relative to cued answers on the same problems. Whole-mode theory: ratio about 1.0. The rival (the spontaneous 'Okay' only marks easy problems or a partial entropy shift) predicts a ratio near the one for non-self-opened plain answers against their cued counterparts, about 0.5.
predictions.recipe: Files: S3 T3.jsonl and studies/rlneurons/results/rln4/t1_t2_items-01/per_problem.json. Self-opened as in the first prediction (first 60 characters of text contain '\nOkay'). S = problem_index values of self-opened T3 rows present in per_problem.json. R = median of n_generated over T3 rows in S, divided by the median of t1_generated_tokens over per_problem.json entries in S. Cap hits are included at their generated length. With an even count, the median is the mean of the two middle values.
predictions.note: Files: T3.jsonl (same fetch) and per_problem.json. R = median(T3 n_generated over S) / median(t1_generated_tokens over S). Even counts use the mean of the two middle values, and cap hits count at their length. The same detector and the same alt detector as k=1 are used for alt_measured. Token-count conventions: in T3, n_generated = n_new + 1 on the rows I looked at (the stop token is probably counted). For T1, t1_generated_tokens equals T1.jsonl n_generated (230 for problem 54, where n_new is 229 and n_prefix is 3), so both sides count the same way. Whether the T1 count includes the 3 prefilled cue tokens is unclear, but it is at most a 3-token difference. Neither side is restricted to correct answers or to non-cap answers, which follows the recipe.

predictions.experiment: Whether a problem's base log-probability of the cue predicts whether the plain base self-opens on it. Theory: the mode choice has a per-problem propensity that the cue's base probability reads, so AUROC is clearly above 0.5. The rival in which self-opening is per-sample noise unrelated to the prompt predicts 0.50.
predictions.recipe: Files: S3 T3.jsonl and studies/rlneurons/results/rln5/map-01/checks.json (key per_row, list T1). Label each problem 1 if its T3 row is self-opened (first 60 characters of text contain '\nOkay'), else 0. Score = cue_logprob_base from the T1 list entry with the same problem_index. Compute the AUROC of score for label: the Mann-Whitney fraction of (label 1, label 0) pairs where the label-1 score is higher, with ties counting 0.5. Problems missing from either file are dropped. Cap hits are not treated specially.
predictions.note: Files: T3.jsonl and studies/rlneurons/results/rln5/map-01/checks.json, per_row.T1 (500 entries, unique problem_index). Label 1 means the T3 text is self-opened by the main detector (empty text counts as label 0). Score is cue_logprob_base from the T1 entry, used as stored with higher = higher score. The AUROC is computed exactly over all (pos, neg) pairs, with ties counted as 0.5. If either class is empty the script prints not_computable, because refuted_by does not cover that case. alt_measured uses the alt detector from k=1. Ambiguity: the per_row.T2 list also has cue_logprob_base. The recipe names T1, so T1 is used. I did not check whether the two lists agree per problem. I also did not verify whether cue_logprob_base is a sum or a mean over the cue tokens, but the AUROC does not change under either, because it depends only on rank order and the cue is the same for every problem.
